artworks.title: Erysichthon Selling his Daughter Mestra
artworks.description: Rijksmuseum SK-A-2572: starving Erysichthon sells Mestra — who will change shape and escape, then be sold again. Jan Steen’s Ovidian scene makes the Thessalian shapeshifter the repeated merchandise of her father’s hunger.

artworks.title: Erysichthon and Mestra
artworks.description: Baur’s Metamorphoses plate stages the father-daughter bargain Ovid tells in Book VIII — Mestra’s Protean gift against Erysichthon’s bottomless appetite. Baroque line keeps her name (here Mnestra) beside the crime against Demeter’s grove.

popCulture.title: Metamorphoses VIII (Erysichthon and Mestra)
popCulture.creator: Ovid
popCulture.description: Ovid’s Mestra — daughter of Erysichthon, gifted with shape-change — is sold and escapes again and again to feed her father’s curse.
